sections.title: Sound of the letter ixe
paragraphs: The letter (ixe) /iks/ sounds mainly like the sound /ks/. You hear it in (texte) /tɛkst/, which means text. This letter has four different sounds.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: To make the first sound, lift the back of your tongue. Stop the air, release it, and blow through your teeth. For the second sound, make that same movement and vibrate your vocal cords. For the last sound, blow air past your tongue tip behind your teeth without voice. Place a hand on your neck to check the vibration.

sections.title: Spelling rules
paragraphs: Before a consonant or after a starting vowel, you say the sound /ks/, as in (taxi) /tak.si/. After a starting e and before a vowel, you say the sound /ɡz/, as in (examen) /ɛɡ.za.mɛ̃/ or (exil) /ɛɡ.zil/. In special counting words, it sounds like the sound /s/, as in (dix) /dis/ or (six) /sis/. At the end of most words, it is silent, as in (paix) /pɛ/ or (deux) /dø/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not voice every double sound. In the English word exit, many people say the sound /ɡz/. Keep the French combination unvoiced when a consonant follows. Also, remember that word ends stay silent. Do not pronounce the final letter as in the English word box.
